meta.title: Services — CROIX
meta.description: Turnkey lighting design, DIALux verification, control architecture, procurement, and commissioning — three packages for developers, architects, contractors, and suppliers.

hero.title: One team from first sketch to opening night.
hero.intro: Design, photometric verification, control architecture, procurement, and commissioning — held by one accountable team instead of four separate vendors.

problem.title: Lighting fails between the trades.
problem.body: On most construction projects, lighting is split across separate vendors. An architect or interior designer selects the concept, an electrical engineer calculates the power loads, a supplier sells the fixtures, and a contractor installs the wiring. No single team owns the whole sequence.
bullets: Dimming protocols that do not communicate

audiences.title: Four audiences. One standard.
audiences.intro: The technical, financial, and scheduling problems look different from each side of the table. Select your role to see the part of the service that matters most.

items.label: Owners & developers
items.title: Prevent budget overruns and rework.
items.intro: Property owners often overpay for lighting because suppliers push expensive fixtures or specify more lights than the space requires. Poorly planned lighting also raises monthly electricity bills and causes construction delays when ceilings have to be opened up.
points: Test the space in 3D DIALux evo before a single fixture is purchased.
Confirm brightness levels and compliance with local energy and safety rules.
Get an unbiased Bill of Quantities and value-engineering estimates.
Reduce over-lighting, equipment cost, and on-site change orders.
items.outcome: A lighting package that is specified once, priced honestly, and built without rework.

items.label: Architects & interior designers
items.title: Protect design intent and material accuracy.
items.intro: You spend months selecting stone, wood, and fabrics. Poorly aimed lights or inaccurate colour rendering make those materials look flat and distorted, while standard electrical layouts clutter ceilings with unnecessary fixtures and glare.
points: Exact beam angles, colour temperatures, and optical shielding.
Custom millwork lighting details drawn inside AutoCAD and Revit.
Coordination with the Milan sister studio, LUMEA Collective.
Ceilings kept clean, with glare controlled before construction.
items.outcome: The finished building looks and functions the way it was designed — without extra drafting work.

items.label: Electrical contractors
items.title: Eliminate installation delays and control failures.
items.intro: Contractors lose time and profit on site when lighting drawings lack technical detail or when control systems are incompatible with the installed fixtures.
points: Reflected Ceiling Plans, Single-Line Diagrams, cable schedules, and load computations.
Control architecture across Lutron, Crestron, Dynalite, DALI-2, DMX512, 0–10V, and BACnet/IP.
On-site fixture aiming, keypad programming, and lux verification at completion.
As-built drawings and maintenance guides for a smooth handover.
items.outcome: A coordinated installation, a working control system, and fewer site callbacks.

items.label: Suppliers & manufacturers
items.title: Win bids and pass compliance.
items.intro: Suppliers and contractors lose competitive tenders or face rejected submittals when they lack verified photometric data to prove their proposed fixtures meet the specification.
points: Fast DIALux evo photometric calculations and false-colour illuminance maps.
Glare compliance reports (UGR < 19) and fixture quantity checks.
Code verification for North American, European, Australian, New Zealand, and Asian projects.
Value-engineered substitution reviews with documented evidence.
items.outcome: A submittal that answers the technical questions before the reviewer asks them.

volume.label: Volume & master-plan tier
volume.body: For large-scale master plans, public railways, roadways, and repetitive hospitality or residential units exceeding 5,000 m², we apply volume-rate reductions to maximise the project savings.

phases.title: What leaves the studio.
phases.intro: Every phase produces something the next trade can build from. The numbers, drawings, and schedules are part of the design — not an appendix assembled after the fact.

items.title: Concept & simulation
items.receive: 3D photometric renders, false-colour illuminance maps, and glare compliance reports (UGR < 19) in DIALux evo.
items.helps: Gives you and your client confidence — and a clear code path — before construction starts.

items.title: Detailed plans
items.receive: Reflected ceiling plans, fixture placement and aiming maps, beam angles, colour temperature schedules, and custom millwork details in AutoCAD and Revit.
items.helps: Makes stone, wood, and fabrics look rich and vibrant while keeping ceilings clean and glare-free.

items.title: Control architecture
items.receive: Control zoning layouts, Single-Line Diagrams, cable schedules, load computations, and system architecture for Lutron, Crestron, Dynalite, DALI-2, DMX512, 0–10V, and BACnet/IP.
items.helps: Turns complex multi-scene lighting into a reliable system managed from simple wall keypads.

items.title: Procurement support
items.receive: Brand-neutral fixture schedules, exact Bill of Quantities, value-engineering cost estimates, and vetted spec sheets checked for thermal and IP ratings.
items.helps: Protects the budget by making sure the right lights are ordered the first time, without waste or delays.

items.title: Commissioning & handover
items.receive: On-site nighttime light aiming, mood button programming, lux meter verification, as-built drawings, and easy operation and maintenance replacement guides.
items.helps: Guarantees a flawless opening night and keeps long-term upkeep simple and affordable.

cta.title: Tell us what stage you are at.
cta.text: Concept, tender, construction, or a fixture list that needs verifying — send the drawings and we will recommend the right package.
